claims.text: Without debiasing algorithms, deep learning models amplify biases present in training data.
Most fairness mitigation algorithms compromise overall model accuracy.
Fairness mitigation methods that achieve demographic parity can result in unfairness with regard to equality of opportunity or odds.
Interpretability can serve as a diagnostic tool to identify reasons leading to algorithmic discrimination in deep neural networks.

evidence.description: Empirical comparison showed unmitigated DNN model demographic parity degraded to 0.347 on Adult dataset compared to 0.386 in raw dataset.
Evaluation of five mitigation algorithms on Adult Income dataset demonstrated drops in accuracy from 0.836 (original DNN) to as low as 0.778 (Optimized Pre-processing).
Prejudice Remover achieved a demographic parity of 0.961 on Adult dataset but shifted equality of opportunity to 0.005 and odds to 0.039, reversing directionality compared to baseline.
TCAV interpretation on a CNN doctorness classifier revealed that not-woman concepts significantly increased doctor prediction confidence.

methodologies.name: Empirical Comparison of Input Bias Mitigation Algorithms
methodologies.description: Evaluated five input discrimination mitigation methods against a baseline multilayer perceptron model across multiple fairness and accuracy metrics.

limitations.text: Post-processing calibration methods require inference-time access to protected attributes, which are usually unavailable in real-world applications.
Adversarial training for representation debiasing can fail to retain full semantic data meaning and is difficult to stabilize.
Current practice of evaluating DNN fairness using hold-out test sets fails to uncover unfairness because test sets contain the same biases as training sets.

future_work.text: Constructing benchmark datasets specifically designed and cleansed of biases to systematically evaluate DNN fairness.
Developing methods for identifying and mitigating intersectional biases across combinations of multiple sensitive attributes.
Designing computationally efficient bias mitigation techniques for large-scale pre-trained language models like BERT and XLNet.
